- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. ## ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

**1. That ID isn't this session.** This session is `f5f727b4-7546-4aa6-9d86-ef229e247d3f`. `652997c6-…` is a different, much larger one — 16,214 lines / 39 MB, last active 18:01:41Z, about a minute before this session started.

**2. You already ran the command.** PID 46600 is alive right now:

```
claude --resume 652997c6-662c-4608-bb47-e37b77ba106b --remote-control
```

**3. `--remote-control` doesn't do what you're asking for.** Per `claude --help` it "start[s] an interactive session with Remote Control enabled (optionally named)" — the session keeps running *in the terminal* and becomes addressable from other clients. It doesn't import the conversation into the desktop app.

What you did get: it now shows up here as a peer session — `ListAgents` lists `zimmermann-pwa-51 [2d733b]`, started ~2m ago, which matches PID 46600 by timing (there's no name→ID registry on disk I could read to confirm that mapping outright). So I can relay prompts into it from here and read the replies back — control, not migration. Its history stays in the terminal.

What you didn't get: the conversation rendered natively in the desktop app. The app keeps its own session registry — `list_sessions` returns `local_`-prefixed IDs with your "ZIMM - …" titles, and those map onto the same transcript files (`local_cb6bc5c2-…` ↔ `cb6bc5c2-….jsonl`). `652997c6` is absent from that registry despite being the most recently active transcript in the project, so the app doesn't know it exists. CLI-created sessions don't appear to get registered there.

Two ways forward:

- **Relay from here** — works immediately, no restart. I send into `zimmermann-pwa-51`, you read the answers in this window. Say the word and I'll forward a first message.
- **Open it in the app's own resume/history UI** — that's the only route to real scrollable history in the desktop app. I can't verify that path from in here and won't invent a menu for you. If you go this way, **quit the terminal session first** — PID 46600 is still writing that transcript, and two processes on one 39 MB jsonl is asking for trouble.

There's also a `--teleport [session]` flag ("Resume a teleport session") that sounds closer to what you want by name, but I don't know its semantics well enough to tell you it'll work.

Yes — and it turns out the last 15 minutes of that session were spent on exactly the question you just asked me. Its conclusion was wrong, and I can show why.

## What the session is

`ZIMM - PR #55` — Aug 18 01:58 → Aug 21 18:01, four days, 480 human turns, 16,215 lines / 39 MB. Touched `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`, `review/SFCC-89`, and a detached HEAD. Spans CLI 2.1.235 → 2.1.239 and has already been through at least one context-limit continuation.

The work was PR #59 (the SFCC-55 footer), mostly grinding through CodeRabbit findings — triaging fix vs defer vs decline, commit, push, reply in-thread per the AGENTS.md CodeRabbit rule. Recognisable turns near the end: *"7 new findings, see what's actually needed, defer/decline the overengineering stuff"*, then *"this nonstop back and forth is getting exhausting"*, then *"why hasn't code rabbit approved of the changes?"* — after which it pivoted to the meta problem and never came back to the code.

**Live state, verified just now rather than read from the transcript:** branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`, HEAD `ec9d161`, clean tree. PR #59 is open, not draft, `MERGEABLE`, `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED`. That's consistent with the session's parting note — CodeRabbit approving isn't a code-owner approval, and you can't self-approve as author.

## Why its conclusion was wrong

It told you: *"The app can't read the CLI's `.jsonl`, so there's no import."* That isn't right. Here's a sidecar from the app's own store:

```json
"sessionId":     "local_7e92366a-efae-459d-9f8a-891edcf99555",
"cliSessionId":  "7e92366a-efae-459d-9f8a-891edcf99555",
"title":         "ZIMM - PR #55",
"model":         "claude-opus-5",
```

That file is 72 KB. The transcript it names is 5.8 MB. It's an **index entry, not a copy** — a `cliSessionId` pointer straight at `~/.claude/projects/…/7e92366a-….jsonl`. Every one of the 48 sidecars in that directory resolves to a CLI transcript in your project dir. The app reads CLI `.jsonl` files as its normal mode of operation; there are not two parallel universes.

The real reason `652997c6` doesn't appear: **it has no sidecar.** `grep -r 652997c6` across the whole app store returns nothing. It's not unreadable, it's unindexed — it was created by the bare CLI, which doesn't write one.

Worth noting the prior session reached its conclusion at exactly the point you'd told it the back-and-forth was exhausting. It stopped at "separate stores" without opening a sidecar to check.

## What follows from that

The plausible fix is to write a `local_652997c6-….json` sidecar pointing at that transcript, then restart the app. I can build it from a working sidecar's shape.

I'd rather you green-light that than do it unasked, for three reasons: it's undocumented internal state, the app is running right now and may hold the index in memory and clobber the write, and a malformed entry could disturb the session list. It's low-risk to reverse — one new file, deleted if it doesn't take — but it is someone else's private store.

Also: **quit PID 46600 first.** That terminal still has `652997c6` open and is writing to the transcript. Two processes on one 39 MB jsonl is its own problem, separate from whether the sidecar works.

Want me to try it?

/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */

# PR #56 — what it put in the codebase, and what it changes for a FED

**17 files, +705 / −462.** Merge `2dfeb4d`, `develop` before it was `b6841a9`.

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` | +370 / −295 — the substance |
| `overrides/app/theme/components/` | +70 / −61 — button, header, listMenu, new `navConstants.ts` |
| `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` | **+6 / −88** — a deletion, not an addition |
| `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` | **+178 / −0** — brand new, the written rule |
| `theme/index.test.tsx`, `types/vendor.d.ts`, `coderabbit.yaml`, registry, projectState | the rest |

**No component code changed.** Not one file under `overrides/app/components/`. That's the first thing to grasp: #56 changes *how you style*, not *what you build*.

---

## Part 1 — The one idea: 237 → 64

I counted every hand-typed hex, px, rem and rgba literal in `foundation/`:

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `colour.ts` | 55 | 21 |
| `typography.ts` | 58 | 11 |
| `spacing.ts` | 14 | 16 |
| `sizes.ts` | 8 | 8 |
| **`zimmTokens.ts`** | **102** | **8** |
| **Total** | **237** | **64** |

**173 of those 237 were duplicates.** The same `24px` was typed in `typography.ts` and again in `zimmTokens.ts`; the same `#191919` in `colour.ts` and again in `zimmTokens.ts`. Change one, forget the other, and your JSX and your CSS silently disagree.

#56 removed the duplication in three places:

**`colour.ts` — primitives extracted, aliases reference them**

```ts
const grey = { 900: '#191919', 300: '#969696', … };   // typed once
export const colors = {
  text: { default: grey[900], muted: grey[300] },      // referenced
```

**`typography.ts` — a scale layer that didn't exist before**

```ts
// BEFORE                          // AFTER
heading1Strong: {                  export const fontSizes = { md: '1.5rem', xs: '1rem', … }
  fontSize: '24px',                export const fontWeights = { medium: '500', regular: '400' }
  fontWeight: '500',
  lineHeight: '32px',              heading1Strong: {
  letterSpacing: '0px',              fontSize: fontSizes.md,
}                                    fontWeight: fontWeights.medium,
                                     lineHeight: lineHeights.md,
                                     letterSpacing: letterSpacings.sm,
                                   }
```

**`zimmTokens.ts` — 102 literals down to 8.** It now imports `colors`, `fontSizes`, `spacing`, `iconSizes`, `motion`, `grid` and derives every `--zimm-*` variable. The 8 survivors are the numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named equivalent — documented, not duplicates.

**The 64 that remain each live in exactly one place and belong there.** That's the whole point.

---

## Part 2 — Components: what changes

**`theme/components/<name>.ts` is now the canonical styling surface.** One file per Chakra component, registered in `theme/components/index.ts`. Currently three: `Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu`.

The rule was established by *deleting* something. `globalStyles.ts` lost 88 lines — the entire `.zimm-btn-*` family (`zimmBtn`, `zimmBtnFull`, `zimmBtnLarge`, `zimmBtnMedium`, `zimmBtnPrimary`, `zimmBtnSecondary`, `zimmBtnIcon`) plus `.zimm-text-btn-lg/-sm`, replaced by a comment:

> *No `.zimm-btn-*` classes here — `button.ts` is the single source of truth for button styling. Use Chakra's `<Button>` for any button, not a class.*

Generalised in the rules file as **one canonical styling surface per component type**, with a reason that isn't aesthetic: a static CSS class cannot express `_hover` / `_active` / `_disabled` / `_focusVisible`, so a class "mirror" of a recipe is structurally incomplete from birth.

Practically, for a FED:

- Every button is `<Button>` styled by `button.ts`. Never a class, never a hand-rolled `<button>`.
- Interaction state lives in the recipe as pseudo-props — and #56 put a real WCAG 2.4.7 focus ring there (`_focusVisible` with `var(--zimm-focus-ring)` and `var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)`), so you inherit it for free by using the recipe.
- New pattern to copy: `navConstants.ts` — when two recipes need the same unresolved value, extract a named constant rather than typing it twice. `NAV_LETTER_SPACING = '0.02em'` is shared by `header.ts` and `listMenu.ts`, so when the designer rules on it, one edit fixes both.

---

## Part 3 — Tokens: what changes

| Rule | Consequence |
|---|---|
| **Never edit `zimmTokens.ts`** | It's generated output now. Edit the owning `foundation/*` file — which is Tier 1, so it's a designer escalation |
| **Scale names are the vocabulary** | `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings`, `fontWeights` are newly exported and are what you reference |
| **`rem` for scalable, `px` for hairline** | `spacing.ts` converted px→rem (WCAG 1.4.4). `borderWidths` and the new `focusRingOffsets` (2px/3px) stay px deliberately |
| **`--zimm-scale-NNN` are class-only** | They exist so `.zimm-*` classes have something to reference. Named scale (`m`, `l`, `2xl`) is the Chakra-facing surface |
| **125 guard tests** | `theme/index.test.tsx` pins the counts and the textStyle↔class mapping. A failure there is real drift, not noise |

The guard-test loosening in #56 is worth noting as the right way to relax a constraint: `TEXT_STYLES_WITHOUT_CLASS = new Set(['button','buttonSm'])` — a named two-item exception with a documented reason, and `HANDOVER_GLOBAL_CLASS_COUNT` still asserted (36→27), so it can't drift further silently.

---

## Part 4 — CSS structure: what changes

`globalStyles.ts` is now a **residual layer**, 36 classes down to 27: typography (`.zimm-text-*`), form-field layout (`.zimm-form-*`), `.zimm-grid`, `.zimm-focus-visible`. Anything that maps to a Chakra component moved into a recipe.

The honest footnote from the rules file: **`globalStyles.ts` has almost no consumers today** — one Storybook demo uses `.zimm-grid` — and it ships on every page. So it's a layer to shrink, not grow.

---

## Part 5 — What #56 did *not* settle — and the proof

This is the part worth your attention, because two developers met #56 and **both misread it the same way**.

#56's visible change is three theme files converted to `var(--zimm-*)`. A developer reading the PR sees "the new convention is `var()`" without registering that all three files are *theme* files. The rules file does say component JSX uses rungs 1 and 2 (`textStyle`, semantic tokens) — but the demonstration teaches the opposite of the rule.

**PR #52 applied `var()` in component JSX**, hand-rebuilding in `sx` what `textStyle="heading3"` already provided — property for property, five times.

**PR #55 built `cssVars.ts`** — a 241-line hand-typed mirror of `zimmTokens.ts`'s key names as `var()` strings, plus `cssTextStyles` reimplementing seven registered text styles. **It recreated the exact duplication #56 deleted, one layer up.**

Same root cause: the layer boundary isn't stated sharply enough, and there's nothing to catch a violation.

Three concrete gaps behind that:

1. **`overrideStyling.md` cites files that don't exist.** Its bridge-pattern and resolver-trap sections rest on `product-tile`, `link`, `image-gathering`/`image-gallery`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, and `theme/components/{imageGallery,swatchGroup}.ts`. I checked every remote branch — **none of them exist.** `overrides/app/components/` on develop contains seven directories: `_app-config`, `button`, `contentful`, `foundation`, `header`, `icons`, `pageContainer`.
2. **It mandates `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`**, which exists on no branch. The enforcement it promises is vapour.
3. **No automated gate knows the convention.** I ran CodeRabbit on both PRs: it confirmed every correctness finding and *zero* architecture findings. It has no knowledge of `overrideStyling.md`.

---

## Part 6 — Propagation: who actually has it

| Carries #56 | Does not |
|---|---|
| `develop` | `main`, `release/v0.1.0` (expected) |
| `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui` (+12) | 10 stale/older branches |
| `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui...` (+11) | **`feature/pdp-token-class-spike`** (17 Aug) |
| | **`feature/f2r-component-registry`** (17 Aug) |

The last two matter. Both were pushed the day before #56 merged, both are **actively worked on**, and both touch the same foundation files. `pdp-token-class-spike` in particular carries its *own* competing rewrite of `colour.ts`, `typography.ts`, `spacing.ts`, `zimmTokens.ts` and `globalStyles.ts` — it's where #56's ideas originated, but it has since diverged.

**Whoever picks either branch back up will hit a substantial foundation conflict.** That's the highest-value thing to warn Han about before more work lands on them.

---

## The before/after, for a FED building UI by hand

| | Before #56 | After #56 |
|---|---|---|
| Where a colour lives | `colour.ts` **and** `zimmTokens.ts` | `

---

## Components: "own the upstream primitive layer, don't build a parallel library"

The clearest signal is a file move on `pdp-token-class-spike`:

```
overrides/app/components/button/  →  overrides/app/components/shared/ui/Button/
```

That looks like a naming violation until you check upstream — `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui/` is a real path containing ~100 re-exported Chakra primitives (Button, Badge, Box, Breadcrumb…). The docstring says it outright:

> *Overrides `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui/Button` via the PWA Kit ccExtensibility resolver.*

So the play is: **hijack upstream's primitive layer so branded styling propagates into every base SFCC component for free** — no import churn, no forked components, no "remember to use our Button instead." One override, and the base cart, checkout and account screens all inherit Zimmermann buttons. That's the highest-leverage move available in a slim-overrides project, and it's the opposite of building a component library alongside the base template.

Two supporting pieces confirm it's deliberate, not accidental:

**A curated scope boundary.** `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` gains a `BASE_COMPONENT_ALLOWLIST` — an explicit ~60-entry set of the base components in scope, annotated by area (shell, navigation, product, checkout, auth, store locator) and cross-referenced to *"the 28 Zimmermann design elements in `f2r/02-design/library/elements/`"*. Everything else in the base template is declared out of scope. That's a real answer to "which of the hundreds of base components do we actually care about," and it feeds the auto-generated `.claude/registry/*.md` inventories that already carry tier, squad and consumer counts.

**In-app catalogues instead of leaning only on Storybook.** `/dev/components` (307 lines) and `/dev/design` (1103 lines) are new pages, correctly gated:

```tsx
...(process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' ? [ /* dev routes */ ] : [])
```

Tree-shaken in production, so no exposure risk. But strategically this is a second gallery surface competing with Storybook, which `components.md` currently mandates a story for every component. Nobody has said which is canonical.

## Tokens: "one source, derived outward"

`pdp-token-class-spike` inverts the direction of truth in `zimmTokens.ts`. What I merged in #53:

```ts
'--zimm-color-grey-900': '#191919',      // hand-retyped literal
```

What the spike makes it:

```ts
import { colors } from './colour';
'--zimm-color-grey-900': colors.grey[900],   // derived
```

That's the right call and it fixes a genuine flaw in what's on `develop` today: my version duplicated every value that already lived in `colour.ts`/`typography.ts`, so the two could silently drift. The emerging four-layer model is:

1. `foundation/*.ts` — the source of truth, ported from F2R
2. `zimmTokens.ts` — purely derived, emits `--zimm-*` custom properties onto `:root`
3. `theme/components/*.ts` — recipes consuming `var(--zimm-*)`
4. `typography.ts` `textStyles` — shared type recipes composed into variants (`{ textStyle: 'linkLg' }`)

**PR #56 is layer 3 arriving without layer 2.** It converts `header.ts` and `listMenu.ts` to `var(--zimm-*)` — but the derivation rewrite that makes the whole thing coherent stays behind on `pdp-token-class-spike`, unmerged, with no PR open. The convention lands before its foundation does.

## CSS structure: "Chakra recipes beat global classes"

The `globalStyles.ts` diff is unambiguous. The entire `.zimm-btn-*` family — `zimmBtn`, `zimmBtnFull`, `zimmBtnLarge`, `zimmBtnMedium`, `zimmBtnPrimary`, `zimmBtnSecondary`, `zimmBtnIcon`, plus `.zimm-text-btn-lg/-sm` — is deleted and replaced with a comment:

> *No `.zimm-text-btn-lg/-sm` or `.zimm-btn-*` classes here — `button.ts` is the single source of truth for button styling. Use Chakra's `<Button>` for any button, not a `.zimm-btn-*` class.*

So the `.zimm-*` global registry is being **pruned back to a residual layer** — text styles, grid, form-field primitives — i.e. only things with no Chakra component to hang a recipe on. Anything that maps to a Chakra component moves into `theme/components/`. Given `globalStyles.ts` emits CSS on every page, shrinking it is also a page-weight win.

## Where #54 fits

Preview environments aren't a CSS decision, but they're the missing half of a design-system workflow: **a per-branch URL means the UI designer can review a component without a local checkout**, and it ends the shared-dev-target clobbering. Combined with `/dev/design` and the registry, the shape is a design-system feedback loop, not just CI convenience. Worth remembering nobody has yet confirmed a preview actually spins up — that PR's test plan is entirely unchecked by design.

---

## Three contradictions nobody has resolved

**1. Two token-consumption idioms, same folder, same branch.** `button.ts` and (per #56) `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` use `var(--zimm-*)` strings. But `link.ts` on that same spike branch does this:

```ts
import { FONT_MEDIUM } from '../foundation/fonts';
color: 'text.default',   _hover: { color: 'link.hover' }
```

Chakra semantic tokens plus a direct `foundation/` import — precisely the two things #56's own description says it is *removing* from `header.ts`. Both idioms are being written this week by the same author.

**2. `var()` strings cost you the things Chakra props were chosen for.** `paddingTop: 10` → `'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)'` turns a theme-validated value into an opaque string: no autocomplete, no compile-time check that the token exists, no failure if you typo `--zimm-scale-3x1`. And `.claude/rules/css.md` currently documents the *opposite* convention as correct (`✅ padding={4}`). That rule file is now describing the old world, and it admits it isn't mechanically enforced.

**3. Storybook vs `/dev/design`.** Two gallery surfaces, one mandated by `components.md`, the other 1,400 lines of new code. Pick one as canonical or you'll maintain both badly.

## The governance picture — this is the part I'd act on

`f2r/` is not a folder, it's **a vendored copy of a different repository** (`Song-DDP-ANZ/Zimmermann-Handover`): 332 files, ~30k lines, its own `package.json`, `server.js`, `vercel.json`, and its own `.claude/` tree containing `settings.json`, `mcp.json` and **git hooks including `pre-push`**. ## What the classifier does

Each emitted declaration falls through a chain: `var(--zimm-*)` → `var(--chakra-*)` → CSS keyword → structural property → **then** the value is normalised and looked up in the foundation token index. Match → this bucket. No match → `NO TOKEN` flag.

So it means: **the CSS shipped a hard value instead of a `var()` reference, but that value exactly equals something in our token set.** Value right, provenance unproven.

**36 is occurrences; there are 14 distinct declarations.** They split into two very different groups.

## Group 1 — `textStyle` and theme expansion (12 of 14). No action.

```
font-size: 0.625rem      ← textStyles.footer.fontSize
line-height: 0.875rem    ← textStyles.footer.lineHeight
letter-spacing: 0.025rem ← textStyles.footer.letterSpacing
font-weight: 500         ← fontWeights.medium
font-family: 'Futura Round', …  ← fonts.body
width/height: 16px       ← iconSizes.md
width/height: 12px       ← iconSizes.sm
```

When a recipe says `textStyle: 'footer'`, Chakra expands it at build time into individual properties and emits the **resolved literal**, not a var. That's just how `textStyle` works — and `textStyle` is rung 1 of the styling ladder, the thing `overrideStyling.md` tells you to reach for first.

So these aren't findings. They're the audit observing correct code and being unable to prove it's correct from the CSS alone.

The `←` attribution reads noisy — `16px` maps back to 19 tokens — because the reverse lookup is one-to-many. Many tokens legitimately share a value. It doesn't mean ambiguity in the source.

## Group 2 — the two that actually matter

```
gap: 3rem       ← zimmTokens[--zimm-scale-1200]
width: 8.75rem  ← zimmTokens[--zimm-scale-3500]
```

These are `SPACE_SECTION` and `SIZE_COL_NAV` in `footer.ts` — **hand-typed constants that duplicate an existing token.** They're the same two Phase 1's mirror check flags:

```
footer.ts  SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'    ≡  zimmTokens[--zimm-scale-1200]
footer.ts  SIZE_COL_NAV  = '8.75rem' ≡  zimmTokens[--zimm-scale-3500]
```

Phase 1 catches them at the source, Phase 2 catches them in the output — same defect, two angles. They should be `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` and `var(--zimm-scale-3500)`.

Phase 1 lists a third — `SIZE_MODAL_SUB = '30rem' ≡ breakpoints.sm` — which doesn't appear here because the subscribe modal isn't in the DOM on initial load. That's a useful reminder that Phase 2 only sees what actually rendered.

## The takeaway

The bucket is **not** a defect count. It's "the value is right but the CSS doesn't say which token it came from," and ~85% of it is `textStyle` doing exactly what it's supposed to. Its real use is as a cross-check: anything in here that *isn't* explained by theme expansion is a hand-typed duplicate, and Phase 1's source-level mirror check is what pins those down.

line-height: 0.875rem    ← textStyles.footer.lineHeight
letter-spacing: 0.025rem ← textStyles.footer.letterSpacing
font-weight: 500         ← fontWeights.medium
font-family: 'Futura Round', …  ← fonts.body
width/height: 16px       ← iconSizes.md
width/height: 12px       ← iconSizes.sm

# Zimmermann PWA — UI Build Guide

Distilled from the SFCC-55 global-footer build (session `652997c6`, 18–21 Aug 2026:
~64 commits, 47 files, 427 human turns). This is the transferable part — the patterns,
traps and methods that apply to the *next* story, not the footer's own state.

Complements the ratified rules; does not replace them. Where this disagrees with
`.claude/rules/`, the rules win and this file is wrong.

---

## 1. The styling layer boundary — the single most expensive mistake

PR #56 established the token architecture. **Two separate PRs (#52 and #55) then misread it
the same way**, which is strong evidence the boundary needs stating explicitly:

| Layer | What it may contain |
|---|---|
| `theme/foundation/*.ts` (Tier 1) | The source values. Designer-owned. |
| `theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts` | **Derived output.** Never hand-edit. |
| `theme/components/<name>.ts` (Tier 2) | `var(--zimm-*)` strings live **here** |
| Component JSX | `textStyle="body2"`, `color="text.default"` — rungs 1–2 only |

`var(--zimm-*)` in component JSX is the violation. #56's *demonstration* converted three
theme files to `var()`, so a developer skimming the diff concludes "the new convention is
`var()`" without registering that all three were theme files.

What that misreading produced:

- **PR #52** hand-rebuilt in `sx` what `textStyle="heading3"` already gave — property for
  property, five times.
- **PR #55** built `cssVars.ts`: 241 lines hand-mirroring `zimmTokens.ts`'s key names as
  `var()` strings, plus `cssTextStyles` reimplementing seven registered text styles. It
  **recreated the exact duplication #56 had just deleted, one layer up.** Deleted (245 lines,
  53 refs across 8 files).

**The one exception**, and it is a real one: sizing props (`width`/`height`/`boxSize`/
`min|maxWidth|Height`) *must* use the CSS var, because the Zimmermann scale is registered as
`theme.space` only. See §2.

**Why #56 mattered:** 237 hand-typed literals in `foundation/` → 64. **173 of them were
duplicates** — the same `24px` typed in `typography.ts` and again in `zimmTokens.ts`. Change
one, forget the other, and JSX and CSS silently disagree. The 64 that remain each live in
exactly one place.

**Pattern worth copying:** `navConstants.ts`. When two recipes need the same *unresolved*
value, extract a named constant rather than typing it twice — `NAV_LETTER_SPACING = '0.02em'`
is shared by `header.ts` and `listMenu.ts`, so when the designer rules on it, one edit fixes both.

---

## 2. Chakra theme registration — what resolves and what silently doesn't

`theme/index.ts` registers `borderWidths`, `breakpoints`, `colors`, `fonts`, `space`,
`textStyles`. It does **not** register `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings`.

| Prop family | Resolves through | Bare token key? |
|---|---|---|
| `margin` `padding` `gap` `top/right/bottom/left` | `theme.space` ✅ registered | Safe |
| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min\|maxWidth\|Height` | `theme.sizes` ❌ | **8×–112× blow-up**, or dropped |
| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | `theme.fontSizes` etc. ❌ | Wrong value, or nothing |

Measured: `width: 'xl'` rendered footer contact icons at **576px** (Chakra's `sizes.xl` is
36rem), destroying the layout. And `s`/`m`/`l` are **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those
declarations vanish with no error at all.

Two more silent killers in the same family:

- **Compound values.** Chakra resolves a token only as the *entire* value. `padding: 'xs 0'`
  is emitted verbatim and the browser drops it. Use axis props.
- **Shorthand after longhand.** `padding: 0` declared *after* `paddingBlock` resets it. Use
  `paddingInline`.

`recipeGuards.test.ts` catches the first two mechanically and is mutation-verified. Run it
after touching any recipe.

**Live unfixed instance:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:302` — `fontSize="l"`
emits nothing. Still there.

---

## 3. `extendTheme` deep-merges — name your recipe defensively

A recipe named `Footer` **inherits SFCC's `Footer`** rather than replacing it. Colliding part
names inherit base properties, and a new key you add is appended *last*, so your shorthand can
reset a base longhand you never knew about.

Hence `ZimmFooter`, `ZimmTextInput`, `ZimmNavItem`. Deliberate merges are whitelisted:
`INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button', 'Header', 'ListMenu']` in `recipeGuards.test.ts`.

Symptoms when this bites: `copyright` rendering 14px instead of 10px, a stray
`margin-bottom: space-6`, a heading gap collapsing to 0.

---

## 4. Component folder structure is NOT settled — build flat

**Four competing structures are in flight, and four Zimmermann buttons currently exist
across branches.**

| Structure | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `components/<camelCase>/index.tsx` + `theme/components/<name>.ts` | `develop` | **The only ratified one** |
| `components/shared/ui/<Name>/` | `pdp-token-class-spike` | Unratified |
| `ui-kits/atoms/<name>.tsx` flat files | PR #55 | Invented a 4th variant |
| `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<kebab>/` | Han's F2R branches | Strongest candidate, unratified |

**Guidance until a decision lands: build at `overrides/app/components/<camelCase>/index.tsx`
with a `theme/components/<name>.ts` recipe. Do not create `atoms/`/`molecules/` folders.**
`ui-kits` appears nowhere in `.claude/rules/`.

Han's F2R model is the most rigorous thinking available and worth knowing, because tiers are
**derived, not declared** — `composes: [...]` in the contract, tier computed transitively by
`validate.mjs`, so it can't drift:

- **Atom** — renders no other component. `composes: []`
- **Molecule** — renders only atoms
- **Organism** — renders ≥1 molecule
- **Template / Page** — page frame; **not delivered by the design system** (Rule F: page
  assembly is ours). That's the cleanest statement of the F2R↔us handoff boundary.
- **Rule A** — icons are *attributes*, not components. A Button with a leading icon is still
  an atom (`icon="arrow-right"`).
- **Rule B** — slotted children don't change the parent's tier.

**The genuine fork** is not "class vs recipe" — it's that **#56 assumes Chakra-component
delivery while F2R delivers framework-agnostic React + CSS.** Both are internally coherent;
both cannot own the button.

---

## 5. The `shared/ui` barrel trap — the highest-leverage override that doesn't work

The strategy is sound: override `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui/<Name>`
and branded styling propagates into every base SFCC component for free — base cart, checkout
and account inherit Zimmermann buttons with no import churn.

**It doesn't intercept anything.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` does
`export {Button} from './Button'` — a *relative* export, which ccExtensibility does not
rewrite. **208 base files import the barrel; 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.**

Verify before betting a story on an override propagating. Related and already in
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`: the resolver is webpack-only, so Storybook and Vitest
silently render the *base* component for a base-path import.

---

## 6. Reading Figma correctly

**Figma reports the glyph box; CSS reports the line box.** A heading measured `h=8` in Figma
(cap height of 12px uppercase) is `h=15` in CSS. Both apply the same 16px gap after it.

So when a measurement sweep shows a **uniform** residual across every element — the footer
showed a consistent +7px, and elsewhere 8/22 vs 18/36 — that is the measurement difference,
not a defect. Chasing it means negative margins and line-height hacks. Leave it.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** Take the *relationship* Figma encodes (gap after
heading, item rhythm) and re-derive the pixel from your own type metrics.

Other layout facts earned the hard way:

- **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line** → `width: min-content`
  resolves to the widest unbreakable run.
- **`minHeight` + `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps** → derive height
  from `lineHeight` + padding instead.
- **Inline-block descender leak:** a block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` adds ~1.5–2px
  per row via the line-box strut. Fix with `display: flex` on the `<li>`.
- **Font metrics move everything.** Switching the fallback stack to real Futura Round changed
  `ORDERS & SHIPPING` 120→106px (Figma: 106, exact) and resolved two wrap bugs on its own.
  Measure *after* the real font loads — the fallback renders ~13% wider.
- A Figma nudge artifact is real spec until the designer says otherwise. Ship it and ask;
  don't silently "correct" it.

---

## 7. The verification method that actually holds

Marcel's standard, arrived at the hard way: **a check must be made to fail on purpose before
its pass counts.** The recurring failure mode was an instrument built from the same belief as
the thing it verified.

The reusable 6-phase suite:

| Phase | Method | Proves |
|---|---|---|
| **0** Gate zero | `tsc --noEmit`, `prettier --check`, `eslint`, `vitest run` | Compiles, formats, lints, unit-green |
| **1** Static conformance | AST/regex sweep of theme + component source | Authoring discipline: no raw literals, `textStyle` over `fontSize`, no bare key on a sizing prop, inline `style=`/`sx=` count, dead recipes, `extendTheme` collisions, token mirrors, base-path import traps |
| **2** Emitted CSS | Parse the *rendered* page | Provenance of every declaration. Catches source that *looks* tokenised but emits something else |
| **3** Runtime | Playwright assertions | Hover, keyboard focus ring, floating label, submit blocked when invalid, modal focus trap + Escape + focus restore, z-index over sticky header |
| **4** Geometry | Playwright vs Figma | Per-element y/h at 1440/1280/1023/860/768/375; wrap and overflow |
| **5** Guards | `recipeGuards.test.ts` | The mutation-verified regression net |
| **6** Review | CodeRabbit `--light --base develop` | Cross-cutting |

**What it does NOT cover** — state this rather than let a reviewer assume: production build
(dev server only — and `fontFace.tsx`'s `assetRoot()` takes a *different* branch under SSR),
Storybook `play` (Vitest never runs them), cross-browser (Chromium only), visual regression,
E2E, multi-site (one storefront, one page), live Contentful data, performance/LCP, manual a11y.

Phase-2 caveat: it only sees what actually rendered. A modal not in the initial DOM is invisible to it.

---

## 8. Harness traps that make a green result meaningless

- **`addon-a11y` is NOT CI-gated**, despite the job name. It needs `.storybook/test-runner.js`,
  which doesn't exist. a11y is a manual gate today.
- **`test-storybook` needs a BUILT Storybook.** Against the dev server the baseline itself fails.
- **Vitest does not run `play` functions.**
- **`extendTheme` does not populate `theme.__cssMap`** — only `ChakraProvider` does, via
  `toCSSVar`. A test calling `css()(theme)` directly passes **vacuously**.
- **jsdom always provides `window`** → an SSR branch needs `// @vitest-environment node` or
  every case takes the browser path.

---

## 9. Static-first is the sanctioned posture

Most integrations are still pending, and UI work is explicitly not blocked on them. Marcel's
framing: *"the build is static-first for now because a lot of dependencies are still pending
but we're not allowing that to block UI build."*

Three patterns exist for absent data. Only the first is correct:

1. **Guard + inert, but perceivable** ✅ — no `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing promises an
   action the app can't perform (avoids the WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4 false affordance), but *labelled,
   not `aria-hidden`*, so screen-reader users learn the channel exists (avoids 1.1.1 loss).
2. **Fallback to empty string** ❌ — `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that still
   carries its margins.
3. **Silent element swap** ❌ — link→button when the href fails validation. The user gets a
   control that looks the same and does nothing.

Never "render nothing" — QA reviews the design surface, so a missing component reads as a defect.

**Guard every href from a CMS/fixture.** `overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts` is the shared
boundary. Non-obvious: the WHATWG URL parser strips leading/trailing C0-or-space and removes
tab/LF/CR **before** parsing, so a browser reads `/\host` as `//host`. A regex without
backslash and control-character cases has a live bypass — that exact gap shipped and had to be
closed.

---

## 10. Process notes that saved or cost real time

- **Commits/pushes/PRs only on an explicit ask** (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #15). Two commits went
  in unauthorised during this build; Marcel: *"avoid commiting without my go signal."*
- **No `Co-Authored-By` on commits.**
- **The Desktop FED playbook and build manual are local-only** — never cite them in a PR
  thread, commit, or code comment. Rest the argument on `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/` or
  `.docs/` instead.
- **Reply in-thread to every CodeRabbit finding**, fixed or not — silence teaches it nothing.
  `coderabbit.yaml:32` sets `request_changes_workflow: true`, so a `COMMENTED` review cannot
  clear an earlier `CHANGES_REQUESTED`; only `APPROVED` can.
- **Stashing before a split commit is dangerous** — the pre-commit hook reads the *working
  tree*, so a stashed generator fix meant commit 2 would have reverted commit 1. Caught just
  in time.
- **Ask before "fixing" a token mismatch.** A proposed swap of `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` for
  `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` would have been a **WCAG 1.4.4 regression** — the token is 48**px**,
  which doesn't scale under zoom.
- **Watch for the audit-loop trap.** Marcel called it directly: *"this nonstop back and forth
  is getting exhausting."* Findings generate findings. Ask whether a fix serves the story before
  queuing it, and present verdicts for a human call rather than auto-fixing everything found.
EOF

Corollaries earned during SFCC-55:

- **Measure after the real font loads.** The fallback stack renders ~13% wider. Switching to
  real Futura Round moved `ORDERS & SHIPPING` 120→106px (Figma: 106, exact) and fixed two wrap
  bugs with no code change.
- A wrapped element takes *available* width, not its longest line — `width: min-content`
  resolves to the widest unbreakable run.
- `minHeight` + `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps; derive height from
  `lineHeight` + padding.
- A block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` leaks ~1.5–2px per row via the line-box strut.
  Fix with `display: flex` on the `<li>`.
- **A Figma nudge artifact is still spec until the designer says otherwise.** One column's
  heading sat 4px right of its own items and both other headings, with no design reason. Correct
  move was to ship it and ask Kiera, not silently align it.

**Why:** several hours went into chasing a residual that turned out to be two tools measuring
different boxes. Recognising the *uniformity* is the tell.

**How to apply:** before treating a Figma-vs-code delta as a defect, check whether it's constant
across siblings. Constant → measurement artifact. Varying → real. See
[[feedback-prove-dont-assert]] for the standard on proving either.

content.text:
Second read done — this one went after the 1.5 MB of assistant reasoning I'd only sampled: 1,517 text blocks scored for UI-build content, 173 qualified, read the top of the distribution.

## The four findings that will most change how the next story gets built

**1. The styling layer boundary is the project's most expensive recurring mistake.** `var(--zimm-*)` belongs in `theme/components/*.ts` recipes — **never in component JSX**, which gets rungs 1–2 only (`textStyle`, semantic tokens). Two separate PRs got this wrong the same way, because PR #56's *demonstration* converted three theme files to `var()`, so anyone skimming the diff concludes "the new convention is `var()`" without registering that all three were theme files. PR #52 hand-rebuilt in `sx` what `textStyle="heading3"` already gave, five times. PR #55 built `cssVars.ts` — 241 lines mirroring `zimmTokens.ts` as `var()` strings — **recreating one layer up the exact duplication #56 had just deleted**. Both passed CodeRabbit: it confirmed every correctness finding and raised zero architecture findings.

**2. Component folder structure is not settled, and four Zimmermann buttons currently exist.** `develop`'s flat `components/<camelCase>/` + recipe is the only ratified structure; `ui-kits` appears nowhere in `.claude/rules/`. Han's F2R model is the most rigorous (tiers *derived* from `composes: [...]`, not declared, so they can't drift) but is unratified and predates #56 with its own full `theme/foundation/`. The real fork isn't "class vs recipe" — it's that #56 assumes Chakra-component delivery while F2R delivers framework-agnostic React + CSS. Guidance until someone decides: build flat, don't create `atoms/`.

**3. The `shared/ui` override strategy doesn't work.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` to propagate branding into base cart/checkout/account is architecturally the best idea available — and it intercepts nothing. The barrel does `export {Button} from './Button'`, a *relative* export the resolver won't rewrite, and 208 base files import the barrel while 0 import the individual path. Worth knowing before a story gets scoped around it.

**4. Figma reports the glyph box; CSS reports the line box.** A heading Figma calls `h=8` is `h=15` in CSS. So a **uniform** residual across siblings (the footer's constant +7px) is measurement, not defect — constant means artifact, varying means real. And measure *after* the real font loads: the fallback renders ~13% wider, and switching to real Futura Round moved `ORDERS & SHIPPING` 120→106px against a Figma spec of 106 and fixed two wrap bugs with no code change.

The guide also carries the reusable 6-phase verification suite with an explicit list of what it does **not** cover (production build, Storybook `play`, cross-browser, visual regression, E2E, multi-site, perf, manual a11y) — worth stating up front rather than letting a reviewer assume coverage. Plus the static-first posture: of the three absent-data patterns, only *guard + inert but perceivable* is correct; empty-string fallback and silent link→button swap both ship defects.

## Stored

Four new memories, indexed: styling layer boundary, component structure unsettled, Figma metrics rule, `shared/ui` barrel trap. Ten total from this session's two reads.

## One decision for you

The guide is a scratchpad file, which won't survive. The natural durable home is `.claude/rules/uiBuild.md`, since everything there auto-loads every session — but that path is **Tier 1 Governance** (both squad leads plus the Integration lead), and we're on `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`, whose PR is finished and waiting on approval, so committing there would pollute it.

My recommendation: land it as `.claude/rules/uiBuild.md` on a fresh branch off `develop` so it goes through its own review, rather than riding along in #59. Say the word and I'll cut the branch — or if you'd rather keep it out of Governance, `.docs/` avoids the Tier 1 process entirely at the cost of not auto-loading.

input.prompt:
You are extracting durable, reusable engineering knowledge from a 4-day Claude Code session transcript (18–21 Aug 2026) in which the Zimmermann PWA Kit team built the SFCC-55 global footer. Zimmermann is a luxury Australian fashion storefront (Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit v10, Chakra UI v2.7.0). The brand is "very particular with UI" and the contract allows no more than 10 defects and no Sev3.

GOAL: produce a knowledge base on **how to achieve and verify design fidelity against Figma** on FUTURE stories. Not a narrative of what happened — extract the transferable method, rules, and traps.

content.content:
### The styling surface for a ui-kit component — decided

**A theme recipe, always.** Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not a co-located CSS file. Pick the
case that matches what you're building:

| Case | What you write |
|---|---|
| It **is** a Chakra component (`Button`, `Link`, `Input`) | A recipe at `theme/components/<name>.ts`. Chakra resolves `variant`/`size` automatically — your component is a thin prop-mapping layer |
| A **bespoke multipart** Zimmermann component | A recipe + register it + read it with `useMultiStyleConfig` + build on the `chakra()` factory |
| Genuinely **static, non-interactive, heavily reused** | A `.zimm-*` class in `globalStyles.ts` |
| Nothing above fits | `sx`, then a co-located `.scss` — last resort, per `css.md` |

**The bespoke case, worked** — this is the one people get stuck on, because a recipe can't style a bare
`<input>`. The `chakra()` factory is the bridge: it makes a native element theme-aware, so you keep native
semantics *and* get recipe styling.

```ts
// theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts
import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
// Figma node 40000265:374 — field/border/* tokens
const BORDER = { default: 'var(--zimm-color-border-forms)', … } as const;
export const ZimmTextInput = { parts: [...], baseStyle: {...}, variants: {...} };
```
```ts
// theme/components/index.ts — register it, or destructuring throws at runtime
export const components = { Button, Footer, Header, ListMenu, ZimmNavItem, ZimmTextInput };
```
```tsx
// components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/index.tsx
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
const styles = useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmTextInput', { inverse, disabled });
```

Note the theme key is **PascalCase** (`ZimmTextInput`) while the file is camelCase
(`zimmTextInput.ts`) — the key is the Chakra component name, the filename follows our convention. Same
split as `listMenu.ts` → `ListMenu`.

**Why not co-located CSS, when plain CSS handles `:hover` perfectly well?** Because a stylesheet can only
see `var(--zimm-*)`, and those are **derived output** — the bottom of the token pipeline. Author there and
you give up `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays, and the
125 drift-guard tests in `theme/index.test.tsx`. It isn't bad CSS; it's the wrong end of the pipeline.

*(You may see `.styles.ts` files using `.zimm-*` classes on the F2R conversion branch. They're a faithful
Figma→CSS transcription and excellent raw material for writing a recipe — convert them, don't copy the
pattern. `.zimm-btn-*` classes in particular were deliberately removed from `globalStyles.ts`; don't
reintroduce them anywhere.)*

### Adding a new token

**You don't.** `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` is Tier 1 and designer-owned (Hard Rule #3). If Figma
has a value with no token, that's a §7 escalation, not a local addition. Same for
`theme/globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2, needs a named owner's nod).

Per-component theme overrides in `theme/components/` **are** yours to add — one file per Chakra
component, registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

### Naming a recipe — `extendTheme` MERGES, it does not replace

content.content:
### The eight things people get wrong most

1. **Interaction state in `useState` instead of the recipe's `_hover` / `_active` / `_focusVisible`** →
   identical in a screenshot; dead until hydration, sticky on touch, and unstylable by the theme (§3)
2. `fontSize="md"` instead of `textStyle` → wrong size, silently
3. **A spacing scale key on a sizing prop** — `width: 'xl'` → `theme.sizes.xl` = **36rem**, not
   `space.xl` = 1.5rem. A silent 24× blow-up that no tool catches. Use `var(--zimm-scale-*)` (§3)
4. **Naming a recipe after an SFCC base recipe** — `extendTheme` merges, so `Footer` inherits SFCC's
   `Footer`, and any shorthand you add lands last and wipes the base's longhands. Namespace it
   (`ZimmFooter`) for a rewrite (§3)
5. Importing an already-overridden component by its `@salesforce/...` base path → your story or test
   silently exercises the unstyled **base** component while the app renders fine (§3 trap 1b)
6. A hardcoded hex or px that "matched the design" → no tool catches it; review will. Reaching for a
   `--zimm-scale-NNN` alias instead of the named scale counts as the same mistake
7. Data-fetching inside a `components/` file → makes the later integration a rewrite
8. Skipping copy-first on an `Origin = Base` component → the override never renders and you debug the
   wrong file

**3 and 4 are the two that a screenshot won't reveal and a reviewer won't spot in a diff** — both were
found on SFCC-55 only by rendering the page and measuring it. They are the strongest argument for the
three-surface self-review in §8.

---

*Verified against `develop` @ `2dfeb4d` on 18 August 2026. Confirmed exact: the 22 text styles, the 27
`.zimm-*` classes, the 125 theme guard tests, the three registered recipes, every colour group and key,
`iconSizes` / `actionSizes` / `motion`, `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`, `NAV_LETTER_SPACING`,
`FONT_SERIF`, `--zimm-scale-500 = spacing.l`, the bundlesize budgets, and all six npm scripts. Corrected in
this pass: several components the rules files describe as existing overrides are still base — see "What's
actually overridden today" in §2.*

*Working document, aligned to `develop` as of 18 August 2026 — PRs #53 (token foundation), #54 (preview
environments) and #56 (token architecture hardening + the styling rules file).

*§3 is the part that moves. Its canonical source is `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` — if that file and
this section disagree, the rules file wins and this one needs correcting. Raise anything here that's gone

content.content:
### Atoms and molecules — where they go and what they're called

**Decided.** Zimmermann design-system components live under:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/
  atoms/       zimmButton/  zimmIcon/  zimmLogo/  zimmNavItem/  zimmTextInput/
  molecules/   zimmInputAction/
  organisms/   (when the first one lands)
               └── index.tsx  +  index.stories.tsx
```

**Naming is `camelCase`, one folder per component, `index.tsx` inside.** That follows
`conventions.md` — these are Zimmermann-authored, so camelCase; the kebab-case rule applies *only* to files
mirroring a base Salesforce file, and there is no `@salesforce/…/zimm-button` to mirror. It also satisfies
`components.md`'s rule that **the named export matches the folder name** — `zimmButton/` exports
`ZimmButton`. Precedents already in the repo: `pageContainer/`, `pdpProductInfo/`.

Three casings exist and each is correct in its own family — don't generalise from one to another:

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Must match upstream; their files import that path |
| **ui-kit component** | **`zimmButton/` camelCase** | **Zimmermann-authored — the default rule** |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream's own PascalCase exactly |

**Which tier?** Atom / molecule / organism is decided by **what the component's own template renders**,
not by how big it looks:

- **Atom** — renders no other component. Markup, CSS and tokens only.
- **Molecule** — renders only atoms.
- **Organism** — renders at least one molecule.

Two rules that settle most arguments: **an icon passed as a prop doesn't count** (`icon="close"` keeps a
Button an atom), and **slotted children don't count** — only what your own template renders. A top bar
composing just Button + Logo is a molecule even though it spans the viewport; tier follows composition,
not pixel size.

If you're porting from the F2R design library, the tier is already recorded there as `composes: [...]` —
use it rather than re-deriving. Add a `@see f2r/02-design/library/elements/<name>` line in the JSDoc so
the link back to the contract survives.

### What's actually overridden today

Worth knowing before you estimate anything: **`overrides/app/components/` currently contains seven
directories.** As of `develop` @ `2dfeb4d`:

```
_app-config   button   contentful   foundation   header   icons   pageContainer
```

That's it. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`,
`list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still **`Origin = Base`** — they exist upstream and are
referenced throughout `.claude/rules/` and the protected-file lists, but they have **not** been scaffolded
into `overrides/` yet.

Two consequences:

- **Most stories you pick up will pay copy-first** (below). Assume it until the registry says otherwise.
- **When a rules file points at one of those as an example, the file won't be there.** The convention is
  real; the worked example often isn't yet. Check before you go looking.

### If `Origin = Base`, the copy-first rule applies

Two of five in. The token agent re-proved every trap live rather than trusting the transcript — bundled the theme through `css()(toCSSVar(theme))` and captured raw output. Worst case measured: `3xs` intended as 2px emits **224px**.

One finding reframes the spine of the document. I had the styling rule as "`var(--zimm-*)` belongs in recipes, not JSX." That's still true, but it's downstream of something more fundamental: **`textStyle` can never emit a `--zimm-*` var, by construction** — `zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse would be circular. Which means roughly 85% of what an emitted-CSS audit flags as "raw literals" is `textStyle` working exactly as designed. **The real invariant is single-sourcing — "is this value typed more than once?" — not `var()` syntax.** An audit built on syntax rather than provenance mostly generates noise.

The corollary is the session's own biggest retraction, and it's a trap for anyone running a token audit: **value equality is not token equality.** Three constants were flagged as mirrors duplicating existing tokens; all three were false positives, retracted three minutes later. "Fixing" `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` to `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` would have been a WCAG 1.4.4 regression — the token is 48**px**, which doesn't scale under zoom — plus a numeric-alias violation, and there's no valid named token in the gap (the scale jumps 2.5rem→4rem). Any mirror fix needs three gates first: same unit, same semantic scale, target is a permitted token.

Both agents independently confirmed `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` doesn't exist while `overrideStyling.md:32` orders you to run it before any PR touching `theme/components/**` — named in-session as "a large part of why 29 literals accumulated unnoticed." Also worth carrying into the doc: `recipeGuards.test.ts` has a **non-vacuity meta-test** ("without this, deleting `components` would turn the whole file green") — that's the pattern to copy for any guard test.

Still waiting on Figma fidelity and testing/verification, which the doc's remaining sections depend on. I'll do a single memory consolidation pass when they're all in rather than editing piecemeal.

# UI Build — Knowledge & Context

How UI actually gets built and verified in this codebase: Salesforce PWA Kit v10 slim
`overrides/`, Chakra UI v2.7.0, Storybook 10, Zimmermann design tokens.

Technical reference only — no roles, no process, no review workflow. Every claim below was
re-verified against the live toolchain and working tree on **22 August 2026**, not taken on trust
from where it was first learned. Where a widely-repeated belief turned out to be wrong, the
correction is marked **⚠︎ CORRECTED** with what's actually true.

---

## 1. How a value resolves

The one-way chain. Each layer may read the one above it and never the reverse:

```
theme/foundation/*.ts      source values, designer-owned — you don't add tokens here
   ↓
theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts   DERIVED output, emits --zimm-* onto :root — never hand-edit
   ↓
theme/components/<name>.ts       recipes, consuming var(--zimm-*)
   ↓
component JSX                    textStyle + semantic tokens only
```

### The registration reality

`theme/index.ts` registers **`borderWidths`, `breakpoints`, `colors`, `fonts`, `space`,
`textStyles`** — and nothing else. `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are
absent. Measured by bundling the live theme and evaluating `css(…)(toCSSVar(theme))`:

```
padding:  'xs 0'     →  {"padding": "xs 0"}                  // verbatim → browser DROPS it
width:    'xl'       →  {"width": "var(--chakra-sizes-xl)"}   // 36rem, not space.xl's 1.5rem
fontSize: 'l'        →  {"fontSize": "l"}                     // no such key → DROPPED
textStyle:'footer'   →  6 resolved literals, zero var()
```

| Prop family | Resolves through | Bare scale key |
|---|---|---|
| `margin` `padding` `gap` `top/right/bottom/left` | `theme.space` ✅ | **Correct** |
| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min\|maxWidth\|Height` | `theme.sizes` ❌ | **8×–112× wrong, or dropped** |
| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | `theme.fontSizes` etc. ❌ | Wrong value, or dropped |

Worst measured case: `3xs` intended as 2px emits **224px**. `s`/`m`/`l` have no Chakra `sizes`
key at all, so those declarations vanish silently rather than blowing up.

**This is the single most dangerous thing in the styling layer, because the syntax is
identical.** `padding: 'xl'` is correct and `width: 'xl'` is a catastrophe. On sizing and
typography props, always the CSS var: `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`.

Live instance still in the tree: `components/header/index.tsx:302` ships `fontSize="l"`, which
emits nothing.

### `textStyle` can never emit a var — and what that means

`zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse would be a circular import.
`textStyle` therefore always expands to resolved literals at build time. **This is correct
behaviour, not a defect** — and it means roughly **85% of what an emitted-CSS audit flags as
"raw literals" is `textStyle` working as designed.**

**So the real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax.** The question to ask of any
value is *"is this typed more than once?"* — not *"is this a `var()`?"* An audit built on syntax
generates mostly noise.

### Value equality is not token equality

⚠︎ **CORRECTED.** Three constants were once flagged as "mirrors" duplicating existing tokens.
**All three were false positives.** Rewriting `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` to
`var(--zimm-scale-1200)` would have been a **WCAG 1.4.4 regression** — that token is authored in
**px**, which doesn't scale under zoom — plus a numeric-alias violation, and there is no valid
named token in the gap (the scale jumps 2.5rem → 4rem).

Before "fixing" any apparent duplicate, gate it on three checks:

1. **Same unit?** rem and px are not interchangeable; rem is required wherever text or spacing
   must scale under zoom.
2. **Same semantic scale?** A coincidental numeric match is not a relationship.
3. **Is the target a permitted token?** `--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases are class-only; naming
   one from a recipe is itself a violation.

Known numeric-alias violations in the tree: `listMenu.ts:17,33,65,84` and `header.ts:59`. Match
them with `var\(--zimm-scale-[0-9]+\)` — a bare `[0-9]` also matches `3xs` and inflates the count.

### Units

`rem` for anything that must scale with root font size or zoom (type, spacing). `px` only for
hairline geometry that must *not* scale — border widths, focus-ring offsets. `em` only for
breakpoints.

---

## 2. Chakra behaviours that fail silently

**`extendTheme` deep-merges — namespace every recipe.** SFCC ships its own `Footer` recipe.
Naming ours `Footer` merged into it: copyright rendered 14px instead of 10px and the subscribe
heading lost its 24px gap. The mechanism is ordering — an existing key is overwritten *in place*,
a **new** key is appended **last**, so your `margin: 0` shorthand lands after the base's
`marginBottom` and wipes it. Hence `ZimmFooter`, `ZimmTextInput`, `ZimmNavItem`.

**A recipe unit test cannot catch this.** In isolation Chakra emitted the correct order; the
collision only appears merged. Intentional merges are allowlisted in `recipeGuards.test.ts`:
`Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu`.

**Compound values are never tokenised.** Chakra resolves a token only as the *entire* value.
`padding: 'xs 0'` ships verbatim and the browser discards the declaration. Use axis props.

**Shorthand after longhand resets it.** `padding: 0` declared after `paddingBlock` silently kills
it. Use `paddingInline`.

**`IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"` as a style prop**, merged *after* `__css`, so a `p:` in
your recipe size is discarded. Size it with `minW`/`minH` instead.

**Register the recipe or destructuring throws at runtime.** Every new recipe goes into
`theme/components/index.ts`. Note the split: theme key is PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`), file is
camelCase (`zimmTextInput.ts`).

**`extendTheme` does not populate `theme.__cssMap`** — only `ChakraProvider` does, via
`toCSSVar`. Any offline theme audit that skips that wrap passes for the wrong reason.

---

## 3. Component structure

**Placement — settled.** Design-system components live at:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/
  atoms/      zimmButton/  zimmIcon/  zimmLogo/  zimmNavItem/  zimmTextInput/
  molecules/  zimmInputAction/
  organisms/  (does not exist yet)
```

Being under `components/` is load-bearing: `generateRegistry.mjs` only scans that directory.

**Casing — three families, each correct in its own. Don't generalise between them.**

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Upstream imports that exact path |
| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream exactly |

**Tier is decided by what the component's own template renders**, not by visual size. Atom =
renders no other component. Molecule = renders only atoms. Organism = renders ≥1 molecule. An icon
passed as a prop doesn't count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom); slotted children don't
count. Porting from the F2R library, the tier is already recorded as `composes: [...]` — use it.

**Styling surface — a theme recipe, always.** Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not
co-located CSS. For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the
bridge: native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`. F2R `.styles.ts`
files using `.zimm-*` classes are good raw material — **convert them to a recipe, don't copy the
pattern**; never reintroduce `.zimm-btn-*`.

The reasoning is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`, which is derived output
at the *bottom* of the pipeline. Author there and you forfeit `textStyle`, the named `theme.space`
scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays, and the theme drift guards. Not bad CSS — the
wrong end of the chain.

**Data-fetching never lives in `components/`.** A component that owns its own fetching can't be
reused where the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, story-mocked, passed from a parent).

### Two API patterns worth copying

**Encode the a11y contract in the type.** `ZimmButton` uses a discriminated union where `label` is
required in both members and doubles as `aria-label` for the icon variant — an unlabelled icon
button is *unconstructible*.

**An affordance absent from the design spec is opt-in, defaulting off** — `clearable?: boolean`.
Adding it by default put two controls in one field.

### Don't trust the generated registry's tier column

`generateRegistry.mjs:122` hardcodes tier arrays duplicating `.claude/rules/`, lists no `ui-kits`
path, and `getTier()` defaults to `4 — Feature-local`. Every design-system atom is therefore
reported as Tier 4.

## 4. What an override actually intercepts

Three distinct ways an override silently fails to take effect. Check all three before assuming
your file is live.

**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` rewrites
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports in the real app build. `.storybook/main.js` aliases the
package straight to `node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it. So a base-path import
of a component you *have* overridden renders correctly in the app and renders the **unstyled base**
in Storybook and Vitest. Inside an override, import a sibling override by **relative path**.

**2. A relative re-export in a barrel isn't rewritten.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` is
`export {Button} from './Button'` — relative, so the resolver never sees it. Counted: **208 base
files import the barrel, 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` therefore
intercepts **nothing**, which kills the otherwise-appealing "own the primitive layer and propagate
for free" strategy.

**3. A conditional render of an alternate module.** Overriding `footer` does not reach `/checkout`,
because base `_app/index.jsx:484` is `{!isCheckout ? <Footer /> : <CheckoutFooter />}` and
`CheckoutFooter` resolves to `pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer` — a different module your
override doesn't shadow.

**The generalised check:** grep for who imports your path *and* for conditional renders of
alternates.

```bash
grep -rn "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

Also worth knowing before estimating: `overrides/app/components/` contains only **seven**
directories on `develop`. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`,
`footer`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still base despite being referenced
throughout the rules files. **Assume most stories pay copy-first**, and expect a rules file's
worked example not to exist yet.

## 5. Figma → code

### The node-type discriminator

This is what decides whether a delta is worth chasing, and it is not a fudge factor:

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Real artifacts measured:
  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against our 45/68 was real, and a blanket
  "it's just cap height" rule would have dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is a
defect. Three contact items all at +7 after every real cause was removed = the heading's cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, deriving from `lineHeight` +
4.5px padding gave 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

### Two files exist — never cross-compare

`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` is the design system; `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` is composed page states.
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page file
produced two wrong conclusions in a row: first "the slot is 59px in both states" (actually
`Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap change 40→24 — the
design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix that suppressed intended
growth when the 68px padded box was already correct.

### Frames are not breakpoints

Frames exist at **402 / 1023 / 1440**. Breakpoint tokens are **768 / 860 / 1024**. The unframed
**768–1022** band was genuinely broken — 18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels — and covers
three iPad models in portrait. Always sweep the bands *between* frames.

### Type metrics

Measure only after the real font loads: the fallback stack renders ~13% wider. Switching to real
Futura Round moved `ORDERS & SHIPPING` 120→106px (Figma: 106, exact) and fixed two wrap bugs with
no code change. `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families and is useless —
compare rendered widths instead.

### Measurement method

- Subtract non-component bands before comparing totals (the footer compares against 476, not 606,
  once the `Disclaimer` band is excluded).
- Measure `y` **relative to the component root** — Figma reports frame-relative coordinates.
- `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'`; `networkidle` never settles on a dev server.
- Dismiss the consent banner first or you measure the overlay.
- `Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths, which *proves* a wrap point rather than inferring it.
- Isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM mutation, one candidate at a time.
- **Mutation-test layout fixes at mobile.** Two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only because a taller
  sibling column masked them.

### A design nudge is still spec

One column's heading sat 4px right of both its own items and the other headings, with no design
reason. Correct move is to ship it and raise the question, not silently "correct" it.

## 6. Layout mechanics

Each of these cost real debugging time and none is obvious from a screenshot.

- **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line.** `width: min-content` resolves
  to the widest unbreakable run.
- **`minHeight` + `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps.** Derive height from
  `lineHeight` + padding instead.
- **Inline descender leak:** a block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` adds ~1.5–2px per row
  via the line-box strut. Fix with `display: flex` on the `<li>`.
- **Gap ownership.** If the design nests a group inside a stack with no gap, don't reproduce it as a
  sibling in a gapped flex container — you inherit a gap the design doesn't have. Give the gap to
  the heading (`marginBottom`) rather than the column.
- **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking.** The row refuses to break, so the words
  break instead.
- **Non-breaking space (` `) is the tool for controlling a wrap point** when no column cap can
  satisfy two constraints at once. Write it as the escape, never a literal NBSP byte.

## 7. Building against absent data

Most integrations land later; UI work isn't blocked on them. Three patterns exist and only the
first is correct.

**① Guard, then render inert but perceivable — correct.** No `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing
promises an action the app can't perform (avoids the WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4 false affordance) — but
**labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so assistive tech still announces that the channel exists (avoids
the 1.1.1 information loss). Switch to the live branch the moment a real destination arrives.

**② Fallback to empty string — a layout bug.** `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that keeps
its margins; measured as a ~64px void.

**③ Silent element swap — the worst.** Link→button when href validation fails gives the user a
control that looks identical and does nothing. It is the only one of the three that actively lies.

Fix ② and ③ **at the atom**, not the call site — one change covers every consumer.

**Never "render nothing."** A missing component reads as a defect to anyone reviewing the design
surface, and the links can't be tested at all.

### Guarding hrefs

Any href from CMS or fixture data goes through the shared guard. The non-obvious part: the WHATWG
URL parser strips leading/trailing C0-or-space characters and removes tab/LF/CR **before** parsing,
so a browser reads `/\host` as `//host`. A regex without backslash and control-character handling
has a live bypass — exactly the gap that shipped:

```ts
const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[�- ]+|[�- ]+$/g;
const TAB_LF_CR = /[	
]/g;
const normalise = (href: string) => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
```

## 8. Accessibility patterns

The criteria that recur, and what each actually demanded:

- **2.5.8 Target size (24px min)** — interactive controls measured 16×16 and had to become 24×24.
  On an `IconButton`, size via `minW`/`minH`; `p:` is discarded (§2).
- **2.4.7 Focus visible** — the ring belongs in the recipe's `_focusVisible`, so every consumer
  inherits it. Note **programmatic `.focus()` does not match `:focus-visible`** in Chromium — a
  test that focuses by script will report no ring even when keyboard focus shows one. Drive it with
  a real `Tab`.
- **2.5.3 Label in name** — the accessible name must contain the visible label.
- **3.2.5 / new-window announcement** — a link that leaves the site gets
  `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a suffix in its accessible name (" — opens in a new tab").
- **1.1.1 vs 2.4.4/3.2.4** — the tension behind pattern ① above: `aria-hidden` loses information,
  a fake affordance lies. Labelled-and-inert satisfies both.
- **1.4.4 Resize text** — the reason spacing and type are authored in `rem`, and the reason a
  px-authored token is not a valid substitute for a rem literal (§1).

**Interaction state belongs in the recipe** (`_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`), never
in `useState`: React state is identical in a screenshot but dead until hydration, sticky on touch,
and unstylable by the theme.

## 9. Verification — what actually proves anything

### The integrity principle

> The verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was
> never made to fail on purpose.

That single sentence explains 22 catalogued instances of a green check proving nothing. The
standard that follows: **a check must be made to fail deliberately before its pass counts.**

**Copy the non-vacuity meta-test.** `recipeGuards.test.ts` asserts its own inputs are non-empty:
*"without this, deleting `components` would turn the whole file green."* All four of its guards
stayed green with `components` stubbed to `{}` until that was added.

**Watch for the shape where a green test encodes a bug as correct.** `✅ contact icons are not
focusable` passed because there were no hrefs to focus — wiring them correctly *dropped* the suite
to 19/20. `✅ locale button inert` was green whether the control was inert by omission or genuinely
disabled. If a test would pass equally well on the broken and fixed versions, it asserts nothing.

**Mutation testing is necessary but not sufficient.** A focus trap was mutation-tested in both wrap
directions and still let focus escape the `aria-modal` dialog when focus arrived from outside the
focusable set. Aim for orthogonal matrices where each mutation kills exactly one assertion, plus
deliberate false-positive controls.

### Harness reality

- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Dev-server runs made four mutation results
  uninterpretable because the baseline itself failed.
- **Vitest does not run `play` functions.** A story `play` is not unit coverage.
- **Every jsdom rect is 0** — layout assertions there are meaningless.
- **jsdom always provides `window`** — an SSR branch needs `// @vitest-environment node` or every
  case takes the browser path.
- **`extendTheme` leaves `__cssMap` empty** — wrap with `toCSSVar` or the assertion is vacuous.

### What is and isn't gated

⚠︎ **CORRECTED: a11y IS gated.** A widely-repeated conclusion that it wasn't ("no
`.storybook/test-runner.js`") was Storybook 8 knowledge. With what's installed —
`@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4`, `addon-a11y@10.4.6`, `axe-core@4.11.4` — the runner reads
`parameters.a11y.test` and rejects on `"error"`, which `.storybook/preview.tsx` sets. No
`test-runner.js` needed. **Don't delete that block.** (It has never been made to fail on purpose,
so it's unproven, not absent.)

**Gated nowhere:** `eslint`, `prettier`, `tsc --noEmit`, any CSS bundle budget. `npm run lint`
currently fails repo-wide on pre-existing errors and CI never notices. `bundlesize` doesn't run on
PRs to `develop`.

`since_last_remote_commit: true`, so a final push touching only files outside every allow-list
leaves *required* suites showing `skipping` while the PR stays mergeable — zero test evidence on

10 moved it to `storybook/test`. Following that line verbatim breaks.

**No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect.** `width: 'xl'` resolving to 36rem blew
